terms.meaning: Traditional first program output, printed when trying a new language, compiler or toolchain.
Metasyntactic placeholder names; their etymology is the subject of the April 1 RFC 3092 (2001).
MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH: major for incompatible API changes, minor for compatible features, patch for fixes.
Looks Good To Me: the reviewer's approval shorthand on a pull request or patch.
Prefix for a minor, non-blocking review comment: naming, spacing, typos.
Work In Progress: marks a pull request or commit as not ready to merge.
Comment tags for unfinished work and known-broken code; linters and IDEs index them.
A proposed change set opened for review and discussion before it is merged.
Git conflict markers: ours above the equals line, theirs below; diff3 style adds a ||||||| base.
Git state where HEAD points straight at a commit instead of at a branch.
GitHub's default branch for new repos became main on 2020-10-01; Git 3.0 plans the same default.
Header line of every uncaught Python exception report.
The shell's report when a process is killed by SIGSEGV after an invalid memory access.
Classic hexspeak value written into memory so uninitialized or freed data is easy to spot.
Not a Number: the floating-point value that compares unequal to everything, itself included.
Binary floating-point rounding in action; the first surprise of nearly every new programmer.
Unix time zero: POSIX timestamps count seconds since this instant, in UTC.
Year 2000 problem: two-digit years rolling over from 99 to 00.
A bound or index wrong by exactly one; its sibling is the fencepost error.
A bug that disappears or changes behavior when you try to observe or debug it.
Explaining code line by line to a toy duck until the bug becomes obvious.
A chain of prerequisite chores you must finish before the task you actually wanted.
The classic reply when a bug won't reproduce locally; the usual cure is a reproducible environment.
Hacker culture's classic editor holy war: modal vi against endlessly extensible Emacs.
Don't Repeat Yourself, Keep It Simple, You Aren't Gonna Need It: core design maxims.
Identifier casing styles, alongside PascalCase, kebab-case and SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE.
The indentation war: PEP 8 prefers 4 spaces; Linux kernel style uses 8-column tabs.
Style Guide for Python Code: 4 spaces per indentation level, lines of at most 79 characters.
Python 2 reached end of life on 2020-01-01; all development continues on Python 3.
Read The Fine Manual: a terse pointer to the documentation before asking again.
Two characters opening a script's first line to name the interpreter that runs it.
Constructs the C standard imposes no requirements on; compilers may assume they never happen.
An unexplained numeric literal in code, or the signature bytes that open a file format.
comp.std.c joke: undefined behavior may legally make demons fly out of your nose.
Debating trivial details at length while complex parts go unreviewed; see the FreeBSD FAQ.
Please Take A Look: asks reviewers to (re)review once new changes are pushed.
Gerrit's top review vote, looks good and approved; a +2 lets the change submit, any -2 blocks it.
Commit trailer certifying the Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1; required on Linux kernel patches.
Mailing-list subject prefix: second revision of a patch series, part 1 of 3.
Commit footer (or ! before the colon) marking an incompatible API change, i.e. a SemVer major.
The two commit types the spec defines: feat correlates with MINOR, fix with PATCH.

terms.text: \ No newline at end of file
terms.meaning: diff's note that the last line lacks a trailing newline; pycodestyle flags it as W292.
Hunk header: old file start line and count, then new file start line and count.
Changelog convention: Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security; an Unreleased section on top.
Requirement key words for specs; per RFC 8174 they carry that meaning only in UPPERCASE.
CPython easter egg raised when you try to import braces from __future__.
Python 2.8 Un-release Schedule: the official word that Python 2.8 will never ship.
pip's refusal to install into a Python the operating system manages, signalled by a PEP 668 marker file.
PyPI rejected new .egg uploads from 2023-08-01; the wheel (.whl) is the built package format.
Free-threaded CPython; PEP 779 made the no-GIL build officially supported in Python 3.14.
Linter code for lines past PEP 8's limit, reported as (82 > 79 characters).
TypeScript compiler error: a value's type is not assignable to the type its target expects.
Rust compile error: a variable was used after its contents were moved elsewhere.
ShellCheck warning: Double quote to prevent globbing and word splitting.
Lint rule requiring === and !== instead of type-coercing loose equality in JavaScript.
Crate-level attribute rejecting any unsafe code; forbid, unlike deny, can't be overridden by an inner allow.
gets() was deprecated in C99 TC3 and removed in C11: it has no way to bound its input.
std::auto_ptr was deprecated in C++11 and removed in C++17; std::unique_ptr replaces it.
C23 adds the nullptr constant from C++11, the typed replacement for the NULL macro.
Nine ??-sequences that stood in for symbols like #; removed in C++17 and in C23.
Size-bounded string copy and concatenation, first standardized in IEEE Std 1003.1-2024.
Python 3.6 added secrets for tokens and keys; random is built for modelling, not security.
One-line, machine-readable license tag placed at the top of a source file.
SPDX deprecated bare GPL-2.0 in list v3.0; write GPL-2.0-only or GPL-2.0-or-later.
UUID spec replaced in May 2024; adds UUIDv6, time-ordered UUIDv7, UUIDv8 and the Max UUID.
REPLACEMENT CHARACTER: what decoders emit for invalid bytes; the calling card of mojibake.
GREEK QUESTION MARK looks like a semicolon and canonically decomposes to U+003B.

terms.text: 0 vs O · 1 vs l vs I
terms.meaning: Glyph pairs a coding font must separate, via slashed or dotted zero and distinct 1, l, I.
Windows ends lines with CR LF (0x0D 0x0A), Unix with LF alone; mixed files make noisy diffs.
The bytes 0x7F 'E' 'L' 'F' that open every ELF executable and shared object.
The magic item that opens every Java class file.
Debug-heap fill for fresh allocations; freed blocks get 0xDD and guard bytes 0xFD.
Magic constant in Quake III Arena's fast inverse square root; its source was GPL'd in 2005.
Last second a signed 32-bit time_t can count (2^31 − 1); the next one wraps around.
Bash: not found gives 127, not executable 126, and death by signal N gives 128+N.
Lost on 1996-06-04 after a 64-bit float to 16-bit signed integer conversion overflowed.
The "First actual case of bug being found" caption on a moth taped into the Harvard Mark II log, 1947-09-09.
left-pad's unpublish broke npm builds on 2016-03-22; ES2017 made string padding native.
Java long-term-support release, GA 2025-09-16; LTS releases come every two years (21, 25, 29).
The crab that serves as Rust's unofficial mascot; Rust users call themselves Rustaceans.
Current C standard, adopted by ISO and IEC in 2024; supersedes C17 (ISO/IEC 9899:2018).
The C++ standard published in 2024; WG21 technically finalized its successor, C++26, in March 2026.
JavaScript language standard approved by Ecma's General Assembly on 2026-06-30.
Editor-agnostic protocol between editors and language servers for completion, diagnostics and go-to-definition.
Habit: keep local secrets in an untracked env file, never committed to the repository.
The rustc analysis enforcing ownership and borrowing rules, checking memory safety at compile time.
Type-driven design: turn untrusted input into a type that rules out invalid states, instead of just checking it.
SEI CERT secure-coding practice 2: compile at the highest warning level and fix the code, not the warning.
Rob Pike's Go maxim: errors are ordinary values, so check and handle them explicitly instead of ignoring them.
Aphorism from The Zen of Python (PEP 20): code is read far more often than it is written.
Pragmatic Programmer, Tip 38: a dead program does far less damage than a crippled one, so stop on an impossible state.
Binary floating point cannot store 0.1 or 0.2 exactly, so their sum differs from 0.3 in the last bit.
Turn raw input into a specific type once, at the edge, so later code relies on the type instead of re-checking.

spec.as: Parse input into a type once, then let the type carry the proof.

terms.meaning: A call that can fail reports it by return value or errno; an ignored one hides the failure until it becomes a bug.

spec.as: Check every return value; an ignored error is a bug in waiting.

terms.meaning: Check data where it enters the program, then let inner code trust what the boundary accepted.

spec.as: Validate at the boundary, then trust the type inside.

terms.meaning: errno 0 is never set by a failing call, so a nonzero return with errno 0 means the error was lost.
The ECMAScript value of a variable that was never assigned; a strict check for null misses it.
The C++ null pointer literal; dereferencing it is undefined behavior.
The digit zero and capital Latin O look the same in many fonts; Unicode UTS #39 lists them as confusable.
Lowercase Latin l and capital I look the same in many sans-serif fonts; Unicode UTS #39 lists them as confusable.
Latin o and Cyrillic o look the same in most fonts; Unicode UTS #39 lists them as confusable, a homoglyph trick.
Latin a and Cyrillic a look the same in most fonts; UTS #39 lists them as confusable, so identifiers can differ unseen.
Known-answer test: the CRC-32 (zlib, PNG, gzip) of a zero-length message is zero.
Known-answer test: the Adler-32 checksum used by zlib for the nine bytes of "Wikipedia".
Known-answer test: U+20AC takes three bytes in UTF-8.
Write the specification first and let it drive planning, tasks and code, increasingly built by coding agents.
Spec-driven development, shortened: the specification leads and coding agents build from it.
Distributed version control system created by Linus Torvalds in 2005 for the Linux kernel.
Git command that shows which commit and author last changed each line of a file.
Git command that reapplies commits on top of another base, rewriting history with new commit hashes.
Git push that makes a remote branch match local history even when that drops commits the remote has.
Question-and-answer site for programmers, founded in 2008 by Jeff Atwood and Joel Spolsky.
Ward Cunningham's metaphor: a shortcut in code is a loan whose unpaid rewrite accrues interest as extra work.
Tony Hoare's name for inventing the null reference in ALGOL W in 1965: a reference that points at nothing.
Bug where the result depends on the timing of concurrent operations on a shared resource.
Standstill where threads each wait for a lock another holds, so none of them can ever proceed.
Knuth's 1974 warning against spending effort on the speed of noncritical code before the hot spots are identified.
Tim Peters's aphorisms on Python's design: 20 principles, 19 written down, laid out in PEP 20.
Jon Postel's robustness principle: be conservative in what you send and liberal in what you accept.
Ending a C string with its null character; a missing or misplaced terminator lets a copy or read run past the buffer.
Freedom from memory-access errors such as out-of-bounds reads and writes; CWE's informal term around CWE-119.
An attacker can write an arbitrary value to an arbitrary address, often as the result of a buffer overflow.
Writing outside a buffer's bounds or to otherwise invalid memory; CWE's alternate term for an out-of-bounds write.
Reading past the end, or before the start, of a buffer; the read-side sibling of a buffer overflow.
Treating all input as malicious and accepting only what matches a strict specification, its length included.
A known value kept in a stack frame and checked before return, so an overwrite of the frame is caught.
Address Space Layout Randomization: random base addresses for memory segments, so exploits cannot predict them.
GCC flag (Fedora/Red Hat) that CWE-120 lists among compiler mechanisms for automatic buffer overflow detection.
Hardware no-execute bit: memory outside the code segment cannot run, so bytes written into a buffer do not execute.
SEI CERT C recommendation: do not use deprecated or obsolescent functions; gets() was eliminated from C11.
SEI CERT C rule: do not form or use out-of-bounds pointers or array subscripts.
SEI CERT C recommendation: do not inadvertently truncate a string when a bounded copy cuts it short.
SEI CERT C rule: allocate sufficient memory for an object.
SEI CERT C rule: guarantee that library functions do not form invalid pointers.
Memcheck's report that a program read memory it should not, such as past the end of a heap block.
Memcheck's report of a free() on an address that is not the start of a live heap block, such as a double free.
Memcheck's warning on realloc() with a zero size, which C23 makes undefined behavior.
